account:
It is day 1, shortly after seven, and I am at town hall with the secretary before eight o'clock office hours. Nothing I have personally observed suggests an emergency or unusual gathering. The secretary has my appointment book and says today's business is office at eight, grain inspection at the mill at ten, lunch at home, council letters at one, tea with the neighbour at three, office at four-thirty, and home at seven. I have requested the book to read but have not yet received it this morning.

The main outstanding matter is the builder's road inspection. Last night the builder reported no confirmed damage on the bridge or east-bank routes, lanterns present, and no spending incurred. The remaining west-bank roads still need inspection. I have relayed that report to the secretary. No repair spending is authorized; inspection findings and identified work are needed before an itemized estimate makes sense. I do not know of an actual hazard.

The secretary relayed yesterday's message to the innkeeper but could not find the baker or builder. That message concerned there being no known gathering or expected visitors last night and no town bread order. The baker and innkeeper's inquiries appeared to concern ordinary bread sales and lodging, not anything suspicious. The secretary now asks whether to seek them or stay to receive visitors and correspondence, and says yesterday's written office record is ready. Today's mill visit is scheduled as a grain inspection; I have no evidence yet of a grain problem or any hidden purpose behind it.
